questions: Is the tremor in your hands worse on one side than the other?
Is the tremor present even when your hands are completely at rest?
Have you noticed slowness in your daily activities, such as getting dressed or walking?
Do you feel stiffness or rigidity in your arms or legs?
Does drinking alcohol reduce the tremor?
Do you have any family members with a similar tremor?
Have you experienced a loss of smell?
Do you act out your dreams while sleeping (such as punching or kicking)?
Have you become more constipated recently?
Has your handwriting become smaller or more difficult to read?
Do you have difficulty with your balance or have you had any falls?
Are you currently taking any medications for this condition?
Did the symptoms begin gradually over months to years?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a stroke or brain lesion?
Are you over the age of 60?
results: 1. cognitive screen (MMSE / MoCA / FAB): MMSE 23/30 and Frontal Assessment Battery 9/18 - frontal/executive dysfunction
2. copper / caeruloplasmin / 24 h urinary copper: normal - excludes Wilson disease
3. genetic testing (targeted panel or exome): NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion - genetically confirmed NIID
4. skin biopsy: eosinophilic, p62- and ubiquitin-POSITIVE intranuclear inclusions in adipocytes, sweat gland cells and fibroblasts - diagnostic of NIID
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Adult-onset Neuronal Intranuclear Inclusion Disease (NIID), caused by a pathogenic GGC repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC gene.

Alternatives to consider:
1. Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS)
2. Spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA) with parkinsonian features
3. Corticobasal degeneration (given the asymmetric action tremor and cortical dysfunction)
dx: Adult-onset Neuronal Intranuclear Inclusion Disease (NIID), caused by a pathogenic GGC repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC gene.
